text:
Pavel Dorofeyev was a 37-goal scorer in Vegas last season, and the Rangers brought him in to finish. He has six goals in 21 games. That sounds like a disappointment until you look at the chances.

He takes 1.62 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, higher than last season's 1.26, and he's put 64 shots on goal in 21 games. Six goals on 9.5 expected is bad luck, not bad play, and goals tend to follow chances. The Rangers have also scored far fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, which has cost him points. Newsday wrote that the Rangers hope he's heating up, and his go-ahead goal against Seattle was a start. Our talent range has him around 28 goals for the season.

He fits the type: more finisher than passer, a player whose shots come off passes across the slot, by Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Our model's closest match is Cole Caufield. Evolving-Hockey liked his defense too, 92nd percentile at taking chances away. He's playing under 17 minutes a night; if the goals come, the minutes should follow.
